description: Statically derived by reading app/cbl/COCRDUPC.cbl, never captured from a run: the COBOL cannot be executed in this environment, so every value below is read out of the source, the copybooks and the fixture rather than recorded from an execution. This is the folder's alphabetic-only rejection - paragraph 1230-EDIT-NAME at :806-840 - and it is driven by a name that GENUINELY EXISTS IN THE SHIPPED DATA rather than by an invented string. The construction is deliberate and is worth stating before the trace. Row 1 of fixtures/carddata.txt is seeded and snapshotted, so CCUP-OLD-CRDNAME is the upper-cased 'ANIYA VON' that case06.json derived; the resubmitted CRDNAMEI is 'Lucious O'Connell', which is the CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME of ROW 34 of that same fixture (card 7026637615032277, account 00000000031, CVV 920, expiry 2025-06-08, status 'Y'). Verified by exhaustive scan of all fifty rows, row 34 is the ONLY row whose embossed name contains any character outside the letters and the space - the apostrophe, U+0027 - which makes it the only stored name this program's own edit would refuse. The point is not a curiosity: the validation at :824-837 would REJECT A NAME THE LEGACY SYSTEM ITSELF STORES AND EMBOSSES, and that behaviour is preserved rather than corrected, because correcting it would be a new business rule. Submitting it against a DIFFERENT, plainly alphabetic stored name is what makes the case reach the edits at all: were the stored name the same, the no-change detector would short-circuit into the four-paragraph skip and 1230 would never run, which is exactly the branch case09.json owns. The three remaining data fields - status, month and year - are resubmitted unchanged from the snapshot precisely so that 1240, 1250 and 1260 take their success limbs and the single message this case pins can only have come from 1230. EIBCALEN is 489, which is 160 + 329 - the width COMMON-RETURN hands back at :549-557, where 160 is CARDDEMO-COMMAREA summed mechanically from app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy as 4 + 8 + 4 + 8 + 8 + 1 + 1 + 9 + 25 + 25 + 25 + 11 + 1 + 16 + 7 + 7 and 329 is WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA at :274-321 as 1 (CCUP-CHANGE-ACTION) + 89 (CCUP-OLD-DETAILS: 11 + 16 + 3 + 59) + 89 (CCUP-NEW-DETAILS) + 150 (CARD-UPDATE-RECORD: 16 + 11 + 3 + 50 + 10 + 1 + 59). So the :388 guard fails EQUAL TO 0, CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM is LIT-CCLISTPGM ('COCRDLIC', :227-228) rather than LIT-MENUPGM, and the ELSE at :396-400 restores CARDDEMO-COMMAREA from DFHCOMMAREA(1:160) and WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA from DFHCOMMAREA(161:329) - the inbound ids and the whole CCUP-OLD-* snapshot therefore SURVIVE. The case contract keys a commarea value by the copybook name and admits the CDEMO- items of the shared area plus the WS- items of the receiving program's own extension; COCRDUPC names its extension items CCUP-*, which neither form covers, so the extension is declared under the one legal name the source itself gives the whole span, WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA, carrying the exact 329-byte image that single MOVE at :398-400 restores. Its bytes decode as CCUP-CHANGE-ACTION [1] 'S' (88 CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS at :281), then CCUP-OLD-DETAILS [2-90] as CCUP-OLD-ACCTID [2-12] '00000000050', CCUP-OLD-CARDID [13-28] '0500024453765740', CCUP-OLD-CVV-CD [29-31] '747', CCUP-OLD-CRDNAME [32-81] 'ANIYA VON' padded to 50, CCUP-OLD-EXPYEAR [82-85] '2023', CCUP-OLD-EXPMON [86-87] '03', CCUP-OLD-EXPDAY [88-89] '09' and CCUP-OLD-CRDSTCD [90] 'Y' - the snapshot exactly as case06.json derived it, with the INSPECT CONVERTING fold at :1356-1358 already applied and the three reference-modified slices (1:4)/(6:2)/(9:2) of the ten-byte 'YYYY-MM-DD' already taken - then CCUP-NEW-DETAILS [91-179] and CARD-UPDATE-RECORD [180-329] as spaces, which is what the :586 INITIALIZE and the :1461 INITIALIZE respectively leave in a PIC X group. CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT is 1 (REENTER) and ENTER is admitted unchanged by :413-424, because :414 lists CCARD-AID-ENTER among the four combinations it accepts. The ordered EVALUATE TRUE at :429 is then gate G30 read downwards: arm one (:435-439) needs PF03 or a done/failed state with CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET equal to LIT-CCLISTMAPSET, and the AID is ENTER with the state 'S'; arm two (:482-485) needs CDEMO-PGM-ENTER, which REENTER denies, or CCARD-AID-PFK12, which ENTER denies; arm three (:502-505) needs CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED with CDEMO-PGM-ENTER, or an arrival from LIT-MENUPGM; arm four (:517-518) needs 'C', 'L' or 'F'. So WHEN OTHER at :535 performs 1000-PROCESS-INPUTS, 2000-DECIDE-ACTION and 3000-SEND-MAP as range performs and leaves through GO TO COMMON-RETURN at :542. Reaching 1000-PROCESS-INPUTS is also why this case names a next program: :570-572 move LIT-THISPGM, LIT-THISMAPSET and LIT-THISMAP into CCARD-NEXT-PROG, CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET and CCARD-NEXT-MAP, so the response carries 'COCRDUPC' as well as the mapset and map. 1100-RECEIVE-MAP :578-636 INITIALIZEs CCUP-NEW-DETAILS at :586 and then normalises each field, mapping '*' or SPACES to LOW-VALUES; CRDNAMEI is neither, so :610-611 takes the ELSE and moves it verbatim into CCUP-NEW-CRDNAME. Two source oddities are preserved rather than tidied. MOVE EXPDAYI OF CCRDUPAI TO CCUP-NEW-EXPDAY at :621 is UNCONDITIONAL - alone among the six data moves it carries no '*'/SPACES guard - and it is left that way. And CCUP-NEW-CVV-CD is never assigned anywhere in the program, because the COCRDUP map has no CVV field, so it keeps the SPACES the :586 INITIALIZE gave it; this case declines to hide that rather than pinning it, since nothing is written here for it to corrupt. 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS :641-715 SETs INPUT-OK at :643 and then finds IF CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED false, so it takes the ELSE CONTINUE at :663-664: 1210-EDIT-ACCOUNT and 1220-EDIT-CARD are NOT performed, and neither is the MOVE LOW-VALUES TO CCUP-NEW-CARDDATA at :653 that would have wiped the fifty-nine bytes just received. Execution continues past :667 with SET FOUND-CARDS-FOR-ACCOUNT (:668), SET FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID and SET FLG-CARDFILTER-ISVALID (:669-670), and then :671-677 copy the snapshot outwards into CDEMO-ACCT-ID, CDEMO-CARD-NUM, CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME, CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS and the three REDEFINES sub-fields CARD-EXPIRY-DAY, CARD-EXPIRY-MONTH and CARD-EXPIRY-YEAR declared at :115-123 over CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE-X PIC X(10) (4 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 10), which is gate G34. The detector at :680-683 is then reached and MUST NOT MATCH, and that is the pivot of this whole case: IF (FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(CCUP-NEW-CARDDATA) EQUAL FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(CCUP-OLD-CARDDATA)). The comparison is over the whole GROUP and not field by field - from :295-301 and :307-313 each group is CRDNAME X(50) + EXPIRAION-DATE (EXPYEAR X(4) + EXPMON X(2) + EXPDAY X(2)) + CRDSTCD X(1), summing mechanically to 50 + 4 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 59 bytes, and that group's date is UNHYPHENATED and eight bytes wide where the record's own field is a hyphenated X(10) - and both operands are folded to upper case. Folding both sides is what makes case09.json's case-differing resubmission count as no change; here the two differ in LETTERS and not merely in case, 'LUCIOUS O'CONNELL' against 'ANIYA VON', so the fold cannot rescue them and NO-CHANGES-DETECTED is NOT set. The observable consequence is asserted as an absence: the 88 at :187-188, 'No change detected with respect to values fetched.', appears NOWHERE in this expectation, and ERRMSGO carries the alphabetic-only text instead. Because the first limb of the three-way IF at :685-687 is therefore false, and the state is 'S' rather than 'N' or 'C', the skip at :685-693 does not fire: the four flags are NOT forced ISVALID and the GO TO at :692 is not taken. Execution reaches SET CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK TO TRUE at :696, so THE STATE BECOMES 'E' BEFORE A SINGLE EDIT EXECUTES. That ordering is not incidental - it is what arms the CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK guard on every data-field highlight below, and a translation that set the state after the edits, or only on failure, would paint an unhighlighted screen and pass every other assertion in this folder. The four edits then run in source order at :698-708. THE HEADLINE IS 1230-EDIT-NAME :806-840. SET FLG-CARDNAME-NOT-OK TO TRUE at :808 leaves the flag at '0' before anything is tested. The blank test at :811-813 - IF CCUP-NEW-CRDNAME EQUAL LOW-VALUES OR EQUAL SPACES OR EQUAL ZEROS - fails, because the name is populated; the third comparand is an alphanumeric field compared against ZEROS, which is odd and is preserved exactly as written. :823 moves CCUP-NEW-CRDNAME into CARD-NAME-CHECK, declared PIC X(50) VALUE LOW-VALUES at :87-88, and :824-826 issues INSPECT CARD-NAME-CHECK CONVERTING LIT-ALL-ALPHA-FROM TO LIT-ALL-SPACES-TO. From :255-259 those literals are LIT-ALL-ALPHA-FROM PIC X(52) VALUE 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' and LIT-ALL-SPACES-TO PIC X(52) VALUE SPACES, so ALL FIFTY-TWO LETTERS, UPPER AND LOWER, BECOME SPACES AND NOTHING ELSE DOES; a space already present stays a space. Applied mechanically to 'Lucious O'Connell' padded to 50, the seventeen letters and the interior space blank out and the apostrophe survives, leaving nine spaces, one apostrophe and forty spaces. The test at :828, IF FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION TRIM(CARD-NAME-CHECK)) = 0, therefore sees a trimmed length of 1 rather than 0, so the CONTINUE at :829 is not taken and the ELSE at :830-837 runs: SET INPUT-ERROR TO TRUE at :831, SET FLG-CARDNAME-NOT-OK TO TRUE at :832 which holds the flag at '0', and then, GUARDED BY IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF at :833, SET WS-NAME-MUST-BE-ALPHA TO TRUE - the 88 at :183-184, 'Card name can only contain alphabets and spaces' - before GO TO 1230-EDIT-NAME-EXIT at :836. The guard admits the message because :384 SET WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF cleared WS-RETURN-MSG PIC X(75) on entry and no paragraph between there and here writes it, so there is nothing earlier for the assignment to overwrite. That test at :828 passes only when the original held letters and spaces exclusively, which is the whole rule, and it is worth being precise about WHICH of this paragraph's two messages is being pinned: the blank branch at :814-819 sets WS-PROMPT-FOR-NAME from :181-182 instead, and that text belongs to the blank-input case, not to this one. Both are 88s on the same WS-RETURN-MSG, so only one can hold at a time, and the one asserted here is the alphabetic-only text - the other appears nowhere in this expectation. 1240-EDIT-CARDSTATUS, 1250-EDIT-EXPIRY-MON and 1260-EDIT-EXPIRY-YEAR still run, and all three take their SUCCESS limbs, so no second message can be attributed to them: CCUP-NEW-CRDSTCD 'Y' moves to FLG-YES-NO-CHECK at :861 and satisfies 88 FLG-YES-NO-VALID VALUES 'Y', 'N' at :90-92, so :863-864 sets FLG-CARDSTATUS-ISVALID; CCUP-NEW-EXPMON '03' moves to CARD-MONTH-CHECK at :896 and its REDEFINES numeric view satisfies 88 VALID-MONTH VALUES 1 THRU 12 at :93-96, so :898-899 sets FLG-CARDEXPMON-ISVALID; and CCUP-NEW-EXPYEAR '2023' moves to CARD-YEAR-CHECK at :932 and satisfies 88 VALID-YEAR VALUES 1950 THRU 2099 at :97-99, so :934-935 sets FLG-CARDEXPYEAR-ISVALID. Their IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF guards at :868, :903 and :939 would have suppressed a second message even had one of them failed, but this case does not lean on that: the inputs are genuinely valid and the three flags are genuinely '1', which is what makes the single highlight and the single cursor position below unambiguous. At :710-714 IF INPUT-ERROR CONTINUE ELSE SET CCUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED, and INPUT-ERROR was set inside 1230, so 'N' is not set and the state remains 'E'. 2000-DECIDE-ACTION :948-1027 is read in source order too: arm (a) WHEN CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED at :954 fails, arm (b) WHEN CCARD-AID-PFK12 at :958 fails because ENTER was pressed, arm (c) WHEN CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS at :971 fails because the state is no longer 'S', and arm (d) WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK at :982-983 matches and CONTINUEs (gate G30, the arm chosen by source order). That single CONTINUE is what prevents any write attempt, because 9200-WRITE-PROCESSING is reachable only from the :988-989 arm requiring CCUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED with PF05: no repository call of any kind occurs on this path, not a read, not a read-for-update and not a rewrite. 3000-SEND-MAP :1035-1045 then runs 3100, 3200, 3250, 3300 and 3400 in that order, and that order is load-bearing for the cursor derivation below. 3100 fills CCRDUPAO with LOW-VALUES at :1053 and moves the two active COTTL01Y titles - line 21 of app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy is commented out in column 7, so TITLE02O is the active line 22 - together with LIT-THISTRANID, LIT-THISPGM and the MM/DD/YY and HH:MM:SS renderings of the pinned clock. 3200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS :1082-1134 runs its ELSE limb because the context is REENTER; CC-ACCT-ID-N and CC-CARD-NUM-N are both non-zero from the :591-604 loads, so ACCTSIDO carries '00000000050' at X(11) and CARDSIDO '0500024453765740' at X(16); and the inner four-arm ordered EVALUATE at :1099 passes over arm one (:1100 CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED, false) and arm two (:1107 CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS, false now that the state is 'E') to match arm three at :1113, WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-MADE - the grouping 88 at :282-284 whose values are 'E', 'N', 'C', 'L' and 'F'. Its body at :1114-1123 paints the CCUP-NEW-* values, so THE OFFENDING INPUT IS ECHOED BACK: CRDNAMEO is 'Lucious O'Connell' padded to X(50) and not the stored 'ANIYA VON'. That is the exact contrast with case09.json, where the skip left the state at 'S', arm two matched instead, and the user's typing was DISCARDED in favour of the stored value - one EVALUATE, two arms, opposite treatments of the same screen field. The day is the exception and is preserved as written: :1122 is a COMMENTED-OUT MOVE CCUP-NEW-EXPDAY and :1123 moves CCUP-OLD-EXPDAY instead, under a source comment explaining that the field is not one the user is allowed to change, so EXPDAYO is taken from the OLD snapshot. Honesty about the strength of that assertion matters more than the appearance of one: EXPDAYI is resubmitted as the '09' that 3200 painted and :1285 renders dark, so CCUP-NEW-EXPDAY and CCUP-OLD-EXPDAY coincide here and the choice at :1123 is preserved structurally but is NOT distinguishable by value on this path - stated rather than overclaimed, exactly as the unconditional :621 is. 3250-SETUP-INFOMSG :1138-1163 is ordered the same way: arm one :1141 CDEMO-PGM-ENTER is false, arm two :1143 CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED is false, arm three :1145 CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS is false, and arm four :1147-1148 WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK matches, so SET PROMPT-FOR-CHANGES puts the 88 literal of :164-165 into WS-INFO-MSG PIC X(40) and :1161 paints INFOMSGO as 'Update card details presented above.' - the trailing full stop is inside the literal - with four trailing spaces. :1163 then moves WS-RETURN-MSG into the X(80) ERRMSGO, so the alphabetic-only text is padded with thirty-three spaces. Neither CSMSG01Y literal appears: the thank-you and invalid-key texts have zero references anywhere in this program. GATE G38, THE CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK-GUARDED HALF, IS THE REASON THIS CASE EXISTS. COCRDUPC does not COPY CSSETATY; it re-implements the error highlight inline at :1243-1307, AND THE GUARD IS NOT THE SAME FOR EVERY FIELD GROUP. The two search keys are guarded by AND CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :1247 and :1257, and their flags were set ISVALID at :669-670, so neither the '*' nor the DFHRED fires for them here - that half of the gate is proved by case03.json, where 1210 and 1220 do run and both keys redden. The four data fields are guarded by AND CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK instead, and this case is where that guard is satisfied: IF FLG-CARDNAME-NOT-OK AND CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK at :1263-1266 has a '0' flag from :832 and an 'E' state from :696, so MOVE DFHRED TO CRDNAMEC FIRES and CRDNAMEC is the one colour item that differs from DFHDFCOL by an error. Its '*' companion at :1268-1272 requires FLG-CARDNAME-BLANK and does NOT fire, which is why CRDNAMEO keeps the echoed name rather than being overwritten with an asterisk - the two guards are one line apart and a translation that confused them would blank the field the user must correct. CRDSTCDC, EXPMONC and EXPYEARC take no DFHRED, because :1274-1283, :1287-1296 and :1298-1307 all test flags that 1240, 1250 and 1260 set ISVALID. EXPDAYC carries DFHBMDAR from the unconditional MOVE at :1285. Two further attribute writes land on xxxA items, which are the attribute REDEFINES of the xxxF flag bytes rather than the xxxC colour items this contract admits, so they are recorded here in the audit trail instead: :1309-1313 moves DFHBMBRY to INFOMSGA because WS-INFO-MSG is not blank, and :1315-1317 leaves FKEYSCA alone because PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION is false. Colours are named by their common/BmsAttributes mnemonics throughout rather than by raw bytes, so a failing comparison reports 'DFHRED' and not 0xF2. The :1238-1241 arm is nonetheless taken, since CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET is the 'COCRDLI' the card list left there, and it moves DFHDFCOL to ACCTSIDC and CARDSIDC - which is the 0x00 that :1053 had already written, a genuine branch with no observable effect, and saying so is cheaper than wondering later. 3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS' protection matrix at :1172-1207 matches the arm group at :1181-1190, WHEN CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS / WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK, because 'E' satisfies the second: DFHBMPRF goes to ACCTSIDA and CARDSIDA, the two search keys now protected, and DFHBMFSE to CRDNAMEA, CRDSTCDA, EXPMONA and EXPYEARA, the four fields the user may still edit, with EXPDAYA commented out at :1185. Those five also land on xxxA items and are likewise recorded here rather than in the attributes member. The cursor EVALUATE at :1211-1235 is ordered and moves -1 exactly once, and the derivation has one trap in it. FOUND-CARDS-FOR-ACCOUNT at :1212 is an 88 on WS-INFO-MSG, and although :668 did set it, 3250 has since OVERWRITTEN WS-INFO-MSG with PROMPT-FOR-CHANGES - 3250 runs before 3300 per the call order at :1036-1045 - so the first arm group no longer matches; NO-CHANGES-DETECTED at :1213 is an 88 on WS-RETURN-MSG, which now holds the alphabetic-only text, so it fails too; the account arms at :1215-1216 and the card arms at :1218-1219 fail on the ISVALID filters; and the FIRST MATCH is WHEN FLG-CARDNAME-NOT-OK at :1221, which moves -1 into CRDNAMEL at :1223. The cursor therefore rests on the field the message is about. xxxL is metadata expressed as the cursor and never as a payload member. Every payload width is the xxxI item's own from app/cpy-bms/COCRDUP.CPY (4/40/8/8/40/8/11/16/50/1/2/4/2/40/80/21/18), and FKEYSO and FKEYSCO stay at LOW-VALUES because the program never writes them - their text is a physical-map INITIAL in app/bms/COCRDUP.bms that CICS merges at send time. Gate G37: the whole conversation state travels in the payload - the 160-byte CARDDEMO-COMMAREA plus the 329-byte WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA that :549-557 concatenates - and none of it is held server-side, so CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT comes back as 1, CCUP-CHANGE-ACTION comes back as 'E' rather than the 'S' it arrived as, and the transaction ends on the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(LIT-THISTRANID) of COMMON-RETURN at :554-558. Nothing is written: validation failed, so 9200-WRITE-PROCESSING is never entered, and expectedWrites is empty as a POSITIVE assertion that no write occurred rather than as an omission - CARDDAT is additionally declared with zero rows on the WRITES channel to say exactly that. The final state pins the other half of it: all three seeded rows byte-identical to the seed, with row 1's CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME still the mixed-case 'Aniya Von' it was seeded with, which proves that no rewrite touched the stored record and that the fold at :1356-1358 is contained to the in-memory copy - 9000-READ-DATA is not performed on this arm at all, so the fold never even runs. The seed is genuine fixture data - rows 1 to 3 of fixtures/carddata.txt, byte-identical to app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt - and row 1 decodes at the CVACT02Y offsets as CARD-NUM [1-16] '0500024453765740', CARD-ACCT-ID [17-27] '00000000050', CARD-CVV-CD [28-30] '747', CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME [31-80] 'Aniya Von' padded to 50, CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE [81-90] '2023-03-09' - the copybook's own misspelling, preserved verbatim, because renaming it would break field-for-field diffing - CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS [91] 'Y' and FILLER [92-150] fifty-nine spaces, the widths summing mechanically to 16 + 11 + 3 + 50 + 10 + 1 + 59 = 150 (gate G19). No normalisation is declared because carddata.txt already ships at its full copybook width; only cardxref.txt needs the pad. The clock is pinned to this source's own version footer so CURDATEO and CURTIMEO are assertable at all, the charset is stated as US-ASCII rather than left to the platform default, and the return code is 0 because COCRDUPC contains no CALL 'CEE3ABD' - gate G35 has nothing to bind to here, just as G32 has nothing (every one of this program's twenty-one GO TOs is forward, the :836 one included) and G39 has nothing (this screen does not paginate). This is case 10 of the twenty this program owns (gate G15), it is judged by field-for-field diffing to a count of zero (gate G18), and the unit is reached as a plain object with no MockMvc, no servlet container and no JobLauncher in the path (gate G51).

fields.ERRMSGO: Card name can only contain alphabets and spaces
